question: Why is testing only the SIP signaling layer with SIPp insufficient for production capacity planning?
options: Because SIPp only tests SIP signaling, but the real bottleneck might be LLM provider rate limits, STT service dropping audio, or agent worker capacity under load
Because SIPp cannot simulate realistic call volumes
Because SIPp results are not reproducible
Because SIPp does not support the SIP INVITE method
explanation: SIPp tests only SIP signaling (INVITE, ACK, BYE). Your actual bottleneck might be the LLM throttling at 50 concurrent requests, STT dropping audio at high load, or agent workers running out of capacity. A true load test must include AI agents processing real or synthetic audio to reveal the full-stack breaking point.

question: Why should you target 70% utilization at peak rather than planning for exactly your expected peak volume?
options: Because 70% is an industry standard mandated by telecom regulations
Because running at higher utilization reduces audio quality
Because cloud providers charge less when utilization stays below 70%
Because the remaining 30% headroom absorbs unexpected spikes, handles retries during failures, and gives you time to scale before hitting limits
explanation: Running at 100% capacity means any unexpected spike, retry storm, or slight increase in traffic causes immediate degradation. The 30% headroom absorbs these variations and provides a buffer for scaling up infrastructure before hitting hard limits.
